title: iPod Touch - Wikipedia
snippet:
The iPod Touch was the last product in Apple's iPod product line after the discontinuation of the iPod Nano and iPod Shuffle on July 27, 2017, after which Apple revised the storage and pricing for the iPod Touch with 32 and 128 GB of storage. On May 10, 2022, Apple discontinued the iPod Touch, effectively ending the iPod product line. The last iOS version to support the seventh-generation iPod Touch is iOS 15.

title: The iPod touch is a worthy end to the iconic music line | AppleInsider
snippet:
While I have an use an iPhone 8, I'm also a daily user of a 128 GB iPod 6 primarily for listening to music as it more storage capacity for the FLAC files I prefer to Apple's formats. Consequently, the iPod is far more convenient for me than using my phone for the same purpose. [...] It was the thinnest and lightest iPod touch yet, but the biggest change was the lightning connector, which replaced the 30-pin connector used in every iPod touch up to that point. It also featured iOS 6 and ran on an A5 chip.

That model only came in 32 GB and 64 GB models, priced at $299 for 32GB or $399 for 64GB. It was also available in several new colors, including silver, pink, yellow and blue. [...] The iPod touch is a product that's lasted more than a decade, and while it's considerably less important to Apple's identity that it was at its height, it's still the least expensive iOS device, and an ideal way to introduce newcomers to the Apple ecosystem.
